spec: The PATH a frontend on the host searches its systempath find rules over — the fact no file on the machine states. ES-DE takes the directories of its own process's PATH (FileSystemUtil.cpp:353-370 @ ES-DE v3.4.1, the non-Flatpak branch), and that PATH is the environment the frontend was started in, which is written nowhere on disk: so it is assembled here from the scripts that build it, each directory in the order the PATH holds it and with a citation of the line that puts it there. A directory spelled with a leading ~/ is under the user's home. Every answer whose search went through this list says so with the note launch-path-assumed. Read by atlas.frontend_path.load_frontend_path.

search_path.citation: EmuDeck's ES-DE launcher sources the backend's functions/all.sh before it runs the AppImage (tools/launchers/es-de/es-de.sh:2 and :5 at dragoonDorise/EmuDeck@863ab69), and all.sh puts $emudeckBackend/tools/binaries/ in front of the PATH it inherited on every system but darwin (functions/all.sh:32-35). The backend is $HOME/.config/EmuDeck/backend/ with a trailing separator (:12-14), so the PATH holds this directory with its separator doubled, which is how it is spelled here.
/etc/profile:18 (append_path, :8-15) on SteamOS build 20260922.1, package filesystem 2021.12.07-1.17 — the session the launcher inherits its PATH from is built by it.

/etc/profile.d/flatpak-bindir.sh:3-4, sourced by /etc/profile:26-30, on SteamOS build 20260922.1, package flatpak 1:1.16.6+r39+g187a5439b571-1.1: the user installation's exports, appended where XDG_DATA_HOME is unset (:1-2 take that directory's instead) and the directory exists — a directory that does not exist finds nothing, so stating it unconditionally answers the same.
